07
Eco-friendly livestock · 친환경축산의 핵심

D2O — returning dung to its origin, the soil

The heart of eco-friendly livestock is what you do with manure. D2O is our barn-and-bedding management approach that treats manure as the starting point of the next harvest — not a disposal problem.

🌾
Odor reduction
A cleaner barn for animals, workers and neighbours — critical near communities.
🦠
Healthier bedding
Drier, better-managed bedding supports udder health and animal comfort.
🌍
Low-carbon compost
Faster, controlled composting returns stable organic matter to the grassland.
Why it matters for Vietnam: in hot, humid climates manure & odor management is the first bottleneck to scaling dairy near towns. Solve it, and welfare, environment and community acceptance all improve together.
D2O · Dung to Origin
08
Eco-friendly livestock · 피트모스 HBP 시스템

HBP — a peat-moss bedding that feeds the soil

The HBP system makes the barn floor the first step of the nutrient loop. A peat-moss–based bedding absorbs moisture and odour, keeps cows dry and healthy, then composts quickly into organic fertiliser for the grassland — closing the D2O circle.

💧 High absorption
Peat moss locks in moisture & ammonia — a dry floor, far less odour.
🐄 Animal welfare
Soft, dry bedding → cleaner udders, healthier hooves & skin.
🦠 Pathogen control
A dry, low-pH bed discourages harmful bacteria in the barn.
♻️ Closes the loop
Spent bedding + manure compost fast → back to the soil as fertiliser.
For Vietnam: in a hot, humid climate moisture & odour are the barn's first problem — HBP is a direct, low-cost answer that improves welfare and the environment together.

Product of the system · A2 hay milk

No corn. No grain.
Just grass.

A sustainable farm produces a distinctive product. Cows grazed and fed on the farm's own grassland give A2 β-casein milk — sold as a premium, traceable brand that funds the farm's continued investment in welfare and technology.

  • 100% grass-fed — no corn, no grain
  • A2 Jersey & Holstein hay milk
  • Welfare-first: robotic milking, freedom of movement
  • Farm-to-brand traceability that consumers trust

Smart farming · BT · 유전 · 수정란이식

Biotechnology: better cows, faster

At L&H Research Center we use embryo transfer (MOET) and IVF to multiply the best dairy genetics — cows that give more milk, breed reliably, and cope with a changing climate.

1Oocyte recovery from selected donor cows
2Maturation & in-vitro fertilization
3Culture to blastocyst, quality selected
4Transfer to recipient — or freeze at −196 °C
Focus: Korean Holstein sexed dairy embryos — improving milk herds sustainably.
IVF embryos — blastocyst stage

Rumen bolus sensor, inside the cow
Smart farming · IT · smaXtec

One sensor. Three jobs. 24/7.

A small bolus rests in the cow's rumen and continuously measures inner body temperature (±0.01 °C), rumination and drinking — the earliest, most reliable signals of what a cow needs.

❤️
Health
Temperature, rumination & water intake
🐄
Reproduction
Heat window & calving prediction
🌾
Feeding
Ration-group rumination & pH option
TruDrinking™ · TruRumi™ · TruAdvice™ — with automatic work lists & SOPs
Smart farming · smaXtec

Smart farming · Early detection

Catching illness days before you could see it

Inner body temperature is the earliest health signal a cow gives. Mastitis and metritis show short fever bouts 2–5 days before any clinical sign — enough time to act before the animal is sick.

2–5
days early warning
40–70%
potential savings via early care
AI — TruAdvice™
The system doesn't just show data — it flags likely conditions:
MastitisKetosisMilk fever
Smart farming · Early detection
14
Smart farming · Reproduction management

Every pregnancy, on time

🎯
Heat detection
  • Reads activity, rumination, temperature & drinking together
  • Heat index shows how strong the heat is
  • Per-cow ideal insemination time — 12-hour window
🐮
Calving prediction
  • Calving alert 15–30 hours in advance
  • Be present for hard births — save cow & calf
  • Two calving alerts flag raised milk-fever risk
📈
The result
  • Fewer missed heats, shorter calving interval
  • Higher reproduction rate = more milk, more calves
  • Less hormone use, less guesswork
Smart farming · Reproduction
15
Smart farming · Health at a glance

Four transition-period diseases, caught early

The riskiest window is right after calving. Each disease has a temperature & rumination fingerprint the sensor reads before the cow looks ill.

Mastitis
3–5 days early
Several short temperature spikes lasting only hours — before milk yield or conductivity change.
Metritis / Endometritis
first 14 days
Prolonged fever periods early in lactation, days before clinical symptoms appear.
Milk fever
around calving
Temperature drop after calving; missed drinking & poor rumination flag cows at risk.
Ketosis
temp + rumination
Temperature & rumination both fall = clinical; often avoided if the earlier disease was caught.
Smart farming · Health
16
Smart farming · Feeding management

Feeding, judged by the cow's own rumen

Rumination time is the truest measure of whether a ration is working. The system tracks weekly rumination and daily deviation for every ration group — fresh cows, high performers, dry cows, heifers.

  • Spot a feeding problem the day it starts, not weeks later
  • Balance rations by real digestion, not by eye
  • Steady rumen = steady health, fertility & milk
Weekly rumination — daily deviation by group
Fresh+10%
